records.title: The Biology of Human Consciousness
records.header: NEUSCI 198 The Biology of Human Consciousness (5) NSc
records.text: NEUSCI 198 The Biology of Human Consciousness (5) NSc An overview of the basic physiology and anatomy of the human nervous system, then explore a series of topics where direct experiments have given us a view of the biological mechanisms that explain high-level brain functions - language, memory, object recognition, the attachment of emotion to people we know and the sensation of time. Recommended: Those with an interest in psychology, neurology, general science or the brain Offered: A.

records.title: Introduction to Cellular and Molecular Neuroscience
records.header: NEUSCI 301 Introduction to Cellular and Molecular Neuroscience (3/5) NSc
records.text: NEUSCI 301 Introduction to Cellular and Molecular Neuroscience (3/5) NSc Introduces students to the physiological and molecular properties of individual nerve cells and the synaptic connections between them, and to principles of nervous system development. Includes weekly laboratory sessions. Course overlaps with: BIOL 461. Prerequisite: BIOL 220. Offered: W.

records.title: Introduction to Systems and Behavioral Neuroscience
records.header: NEUSCI 302 Introduction to Systems and Behavioral Neuroscience (3/5) NSc
records.text: NEUSCI 302 Introduction to Systems and Behavioral Neuroscience (3/5) NSc Introduces neuroethology, i.e., the mechanisms by which neurons and the synaptic connections among them produce sensory perceptions and complex behavioral outputs. Available with or without weekly laboratory sessions. Course overlaps with: BIOL 459; T BIOL 312; and T BIOL 412. Prerequisite: NEUSCI 301. Offered: A.

records.title: Systems Neuroscience
records.text: NEUSCI 401 Systems Neuroscience (3) NSc Introduces students to the anatomical and physiological organization of the major sensory, motor, and associative systems of the mammalian brain. Behavioral data used to stress functional integration of systems. Includes gross brain anatomy demonstration and computer tutorials. Course overlaps with: T BIOL 312. Prerequisite: NEUSCI 301. Offered: Sp.

records.title: Diseases of the Nervous System
records.header: NEUSCI 402 Diseases of the Nervous System (3) NSc
records.text: NEUSCI 402 Diseases of the Nervous System (3) NSc Introduces the basic mechanisms of mammalian nervous system function through the study of human neurological diseases that result from specific disruption of neuronal signaling. Course overlaps with: B BIO 390. Prerequisite: NEUSCI 401. Offered: W.

records.title: Computational Models for Cognitive Neuroscience
records.header: NEUSCI 403 Computational Models for Cognitive Neuroscience (3) NSc
records.text: NEUSCI 403 Computational Models for Cognitive Neuroscience (3) NSc Introduces some of the most fundamental concepts of computational models as applied to Cognitive Neuroscience. These models aim at providing explanations of how complex behavior can arise from simple algorithms that are implemented at the neuronal level. Prerequisite: NEUSCI 401. Offered: W.

records.title: Neuropharmacology
records.text: NEUSCI 404 Neuropharmacology (3) NSc Actions of drugs on the brain at clinical, cellular, and molecular levels. Therapeutic use of drugs in treatment of neurological and psychiatric diseases. Abuse of drugs and the mechanisms of addiction, tolerance, and withdrawal. Course overlaps with: B BIO 390 and TPSYCH 361/T BIOL 361. Prerequisite: NEUSCI 401. Offered: Sp.

records.title: Quantitative Methods in Neuroscience
records.header: NEUSCI 445 Quantitative Methods in Neuroscience (3) NSc
records.text: NEUSCI 445 Quantitative Methods in Neuroscience (3) NSc Quantitative methods applicable to study of the nervous system. Emphasizes computer exercises/discussion of journal papers.
